facts.fact: The civil status law adopted on 25 October 2023 makes the ministry in charge of civil status responsible for designing and producing the recording media, buying, installing and maintaining the equipment and delivering it to the civil status centres (art. 65), and charges principal centres with the entry and electronic archiving of the civil status data they register (art. 59).
facts.system: système d'enregistrement des faits d'état civil / registre national de l'état civil

systems.system: registre de l'état civil ou système d'enregistrement des faits d'état civil; registre national de l'état civil
systems.owner: ministry in charge of civil status; officers of civil status (mayors) under the public prosecutor
systems.tiers: in law: principal centres at the seats of urban and rural communes, embassies and consulates; secondary centres in quarters, districts and villages

systems.system: centres de déclaration and carnets de déclaration
systems.country_label: centre de déclaration des faits d'état civil; agent de déclaration
systems.owner: commune (contract agent), under the principal and secondary centre heads
systems.tiers: in law: public and private health facilities, places of worship, cemeteries, villages, districts and quarters

note: A statute, held as an excerpt ending in art. 88: it states what the law provides, not what offices do. It allows both paper and electronic recording media (art. 63), says declaration, registration and delivery are done by electronic processes (art. 8), yet requires acts to be written in indelible ink in secured duplicate registers supplied by the ministry (arts. 39-40), and leaves electronic management rules to a decree; no made, events or offices fact is taken from it.
